   362→static FASTCALL_ATTR JSOBJ FASTCALL_MSVC decode_string ( struct DecoderState *ds)
   363→{
   364→  int index;
   365→  JSUINT32 *escOffset;
   366→  JSUINT32 *escStart;
   367→  size_t escLen = (ds->escEnd - ds->escStart);
   368→  JSUINT8 *inputOffset;
   369→  JSUTF16 ch = 0;
   370→  JSUINT8 *lastHighSurrogate = NULL;
   371→  JSUINT8 oct;
   372→  JSUTF32 ucs;
   373→  ds->lastType = JT_INVALID;
   374→  ds->start ++;
   375→
   376→  if ( (size_t) (ds->end - ds->start) > escLen)
   377→  {
   378→    size_t newSize = (ds->end - ds->start);
   379→
   380→    if (ds->escHeap)
   381→    {
   382→      if (newSize > (SIZE_MAX / sizeof(JSUINT32)))
   383→      {
   384→        return SetError(ds, -1, "Could not reserve memory block");
   385→      }
   386→      escStart = (JSUINT32 *)ds->dec->realloc(ds->escStart, newSize * sizeof(JSUINT32));
   387→      if (!escStart)
   388→      {
   389→        // Don't free ds->escStart here; it gets handled in JSON_DecodeObject.
   390→        return SetError(ds, -1, "Could not reserve memory block");
   391→      }
   392→      ds->escStart = escStart;
   393→    }
   394→    else
   395→    {
   396→      JSUINT32 *oldStart = ds->escStart;
   397→      if (newSize > (SIZE_MAX / sizeof(JSUINT32)))
   398→      {
   399→        return SetError(ds, -1, "Could not reserve memory block");
   400→      }
   401→      ds->escStart = (JSUINT32 *) ds->dec->malloc(newSize * sizeof(JSUINT32));
   402→      if (!ds->escStart)
   403→      {
   404→        return SetError(ds, -1, "Could not reserve memory block");
   405→      }
   406→      ds->escHeap = 1;
   407→      memcpy(ds->escStart, oldStart, escLen * sizeof(JSUINT32));
   408→    }
   409→
   410→    ds->escEnd = ds->escStart + newSize;
   411→  }
   412→
   413→  escOffset = ds->escStart;
   414→  inputOffset = (JSUINT8 *) ds->start;
   415→
   416→  for (;;)
   417→  {
   418→    switch (g_decoderLookup[(JSUINT8)(*inputOffset)])
   419→    {
   420→      case DS_ISNULL:
   421→      {
   422→        return SetError(ds, -1, "Unmatched '\"' when decoding 'string'");
   423→      }
   424→      case DS_ISQUOTE:
   425→      {
   426→        ds->lastType = JT_UTF8;
   427→        inputOffset ++;
   428→        ds->start += ( (char *) inputOffset - (ds->start));
   429→        return ds->dec->newString(ds->prv, ds->escStart, escOffset);
   430→      }
   431→      case DS_UTFLENERROR:
   432→      {
   433→        return SetError (ds, -1, "Invalid UTF-8 sequence length when decoding 'string'");
   434→      }
   435→      case DS_ISESCAPE:
   436→      {
   437→        inputOffset ++;
   438→        switch (*inputOffset)
   439→        {
   440→          case '\\': *(escOffset++) = '\\'; inputOffset++; continue;
   441→          case '\"': *(escOffset++) = '\"'; inputOffset++; continue;
   442→          case '/':  *(escOffset++) = '/';  inputOffset++; continue;
   443→          case 'b':  *(escOffset++) = '\b'; inputOffset++; continue;
   444→          case 'f':  *(escOffset++) = '\f'; inputOffset++; continue;
   445→          case 'n':  *(escOffset++) = '\n'; inputOffset++; continue;
   446→          case 'r':  *(escOffset++) = '\r'; inputOffset++; continue;
   447→          case 't':  *(escOffset++) = '\t'; inputOffset++; continue;
   448→
   449→          case 'u':
   450→          {
   451→            int index;
   452→            inputOffset ++;
   453→
   454→            for (index = 0; index < 4; index ++)
   455→            {
   456→              switch (*inputOffset)
   457→              {
   458→                case '\0': return SetError (ds, -1, "Unterminated unicode escape sequence when decoding 'string'");
   459→                default: return SetError (ds, -1, "Unexpected character in unicode escape sequence when decoding 'string'");
   460→
   461→                case '0':
   462→                case '1':
   463→                case '2':
   464→                case '3':
   465→                case '4':
   466→                case '5':
   467→                case '6':
   468→                case '7':
   469→                case '8':
   470→                case '9':
   471→                  ch = (ch << 4) + (JSUTF16) (*inputOffset - '0');
   472→                  break;
   473→
   474→                case 'a':
   475→                case 'b':
   476→                case 'c':
   477→                case 'd':
   478→                case 'e':
   479→                case 'f':
   480→                  ch = (ch << 4) + 10 + (JSUTF16) (*inputOffset - 'a');
   481→                  break;
   482→
   483→                case 'A':
   484→                case 'B':
   485→                case 'C':
   486→                case 'D':
   487→                case 'E':
   488→                case 'F':
   489→                  ch = (ch << 4) + 10 + (JSUTF16) (*inputOffset - 'A');
   490→                  break;
   491→              }
   492→
   493→              inputOffset ++;
   494→            }
   495→
   496→            if ((ch & 0xfc00) == 0xdc00 && lastHighSurrogate == inputOffset - 6 * sizeof(*inputOffset))
   497→            {
   498→              // Low surrogate immediately following a high surrogate
   499→              // Overwrite existing high surrogate with combined character
   500→              *(escOffset-1) = (((*(escOffset-1) - 0xd800) <<10) | (ch - 0xdc00)) + 0x10000;
   501→            }
   502→            else
   503→            {
   504→              *(escOffset++) = (JSUINT32) ch;
   505→            }
   506→            if ((ch & 0xfc00) == 0xd800)
   507→            {
   508→              lastHighSurrogate = inputOffset;
   509→            }
   510→            break;
   511→          }
   512→
   513→          case '\0': return SetError(ds, -1, "Unterminated escape sequence when decoding 'string'");
   514→          default: return SetError(ds, -1, "Unrecognized escape sequence when decoding 'string'");
   515→        }
   516→        break;
   517→      }
   518→
   519→      case 1:
   520→      {
   521→        *(escOffset++) = (JSUINT32) (*inputOffset++);
   522→        break;
   523→      }
   524→
   525→      case 2:
   526→      {
   527→        ucs = (*inputOffset++) & 0x1f;
   528→        ucs <<= 6;
   529→        if (((*inputOffset) & 0x80) != 0x80)
   530→        {
   531→          return SetError(ds, -1, "Invalid octet in UTF-8 sequence when decoding 'string'");
   532→        }
   533→        ucs |= (*inputOffset++) & 0x3f;
   534→        if (ucs < 0x80) return SetError (ds, -1, "Overlong 2 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when decoding 'string'");
   535→        *(escOffset++) = (JSUINT32) ucs;
   536→        break;
   537→      }
   538→
   539→      case 3:
   540→      {
   541→        JSUTF32 ucs = 0;
   542→        ucs |= (*inputOffset++) & 0x0f;
   543→
   544→        for (index = 0; index < 2; index ++)
   545→        {
   546→          ucs <<= 6;
   547→          oct = (*inputOffset++);
   548→
   549→          if ((oct & 0x80) != 0x80)
   550→          {
   551→            return SetError(ds, -1, "Invalid octet in UTF-8 sequence when decoding 'string'");
   552→          }
   553→
   554→          ucs |= oct & 0x3f;
   555→        }
   556→
   557→        if (ucs < 0x800) return SetError (ds, -1, "Overlong 3 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when encoding string");
   558→        *(escOffset++) = (JSUINT32) ucs;
   559→        break;
   560→      }
   561→
   562→      case 4:
   563→      {
   564→        JSUTF32 ucs = 0;
   565→        ucs |= (*inputOffset++) & 0x07;
   566→
   567→        for (index = 0; index < 3; index ++)
   568→        {
   569→          ucs <<= 6;
   570→          oct = (*inputOffset++);
   571→
   572→          if ((oct & 0x80) != 0x80)
   573→          {
   574→            return SetError(ds, -1, "Invalid octet in UTF-8 sequence when decoding 'string'");
   575→          }
   576→
   577→          ucs |= oct & 0x3f;
   578→        }
   579→
   580→        if (ucs < 0x10000) return SetError (ds, -1, "Overlong 4 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when decoding 'string'");
   581→
   582→        *(escOffset++) = (JSUINT32) ucs;
   583→        break;
   584→      }
   585→    }
   586→  }
   587→}

   589→static FASTCALL_ATTR JSOBJ FASTCALL_MSVC decode_array(struct DecoderState *ds)
   590→{
   591→  JSOBJ itemValue;
   592→  JSOBJ newObj;
   593→  int len;
   594→  ds->objDepth++;
   595→  if (ds->objDepth > JSON_MAX_OBJECT_DEPTH) {
   596→    return SetError(ds, -1, "Reached object decoding depth limit");
   597→  }
   598→
   599→  newObj = ds->dec->newArray(ds->prv);
   600→  len = 0;
   601→
   602→  ds->lastType = JT_INVALID;
   603→  ds->start ++;
   604→
   605→  for (;;)
   606→  {
   607→    SkipWhitespace(ds);
   608→
   609→    if ((*ds->start) == ']')
   610→    {
   611→      ds->objDepth--;
   612→      if (len == 0)
   613→      {
   614→        ds->start ++;
   615→        return newObj;
   616→      }
   617→
   618→      ds->dec->releaseObject(ds->prv, newObj);
   619→      return SetError(ds, -1, "Unexpected character found when decoding array value (1)");
   620→    }
   621→
   622→    itemValue = decode_any(ds);
   623→
   624→    if (itemValue == NULL)
   625→    {
   626→      ds->dec->releaseObject(ds->prv, newObj);
   627→      return NULL;
   628→    }
   629→
   630→    ds->dec->arrayAddItem (ds->prv, newObj, itemValue);
   631→
   632→    SkipWhitespace(ds);
   633→
   634→    switch (*(ds->start++))
   635→    {
   636→    case ']':
   637→    {
   638→      ds->objDepth--;
   639→      return newObj;
   640→    }
   641→    case ',':
   642→      break;
   643→
   644→    default:
   645→      ds->dec->releaseObject(ds->prv, newObj);
   646→      return SetError(ds, -1, "Unexpected character found when decoding array value (2)");
   647→    }
   648→
   649→    len++;
   650→  }
   651→}

   653→static FASTCALL_ATTR JSOBJ FASTCALL_MSVC decode_object( struct DecoderState *ds)
   654→{
   655→  JSOBJ itemName;
   656→  JSOBJ itemValue;
   657→  JSOBJ newObj;
   658→  int len;
   659→
   660→  ds->objDepth++;
   661→  if (ds->objDepth > JSON_MAX_OBJECT_DEPTH)
   662→  {
   663→    return SetError(ds, -1, "Reached object decoding depth limit");
   664→  }
   665→
   666→  newObj = ds->dec->newObject(ds->prv);
   667→  len = 0;
   668→
   669→  ds->start ++;
   670→
   671→  for (;;)
   672→  {
   673→    SkipWhitespace(ds);
   674→
   675→    if ((*ds->start) == '}')
   676→    {
   677→      ds->objDepth--;
   678→      if (len == 0)
   679→      {
   680→        ds->start ++;
   681→        return newObj;
   682→      }
   683→
   684→      ds->dec->releaseObject(ds->prv, newObj);
   685→      return SetError(ds, -1, "Unexpected character in found when decoding object value");
   686→    }

  3. If input is str (PyUnicode): encodes to UTF-8 via PyUnicode_AsEncodedString

  - The decoder handles: strings with escape sequences (\uXXXX, \n, etc.),

     2→
     3→[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/ujson.svg?logo=pypi&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     4→[![Supported Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/ujson.svg?logo=python&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     5→[![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/ujson.svg)](https://pypistats.org/packages/ujson)
     6→[![GitHub Actions status](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/workflows/Test/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/actions)
     7→[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson)
     8→[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/1418941.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1418941)
     9→[![Code style: Black](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-Black-000000.svg)](https://github.com/psf/black)
    10→
    11→UltraJSON is an ultra fast JSON encoder and decoder written in pure C with bindings for
    12→Python.
    13→
    14→Install with pip:
    15→
    16→```sh
    17→python -m pip install ujson
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Project status
    21→
    22→> [!WARNING]
    23→> UltraJSON's architecture is fundamentally ill-suited to making changes without
    24→> risk of introducing new security vulnerabilities. As a result, this library
    25→> has been put into a *maintenance-only* mode. Support for new Python versions
    26→> will be added and critical bugs and security issues will still be
    27→> fixed but all other changes will be rejected. Users are encouraged to migrate
    28→> to [orjson](https://pypi.org/project/orjson/) which is both much faster and
    29→> less likely to introduce a surprise buffer overflow vulnerability in the
    30→> future.
    31→
    32→## Usage
    33→
    34→May be used as a drop in replacement for most other JSON parsers for Python:
    35→
    36→```pycon
    37→>>> import ujson
    38→>>> ujson.dumps([{"key": "value"}, 81, True])
    39→'[{"key":"value"},81,true]'
    40→>>> ujson.loads("""[{"key": "value"}, 81, true]""")
    41→[{'key': 'value'}, 81, True]
    42→```
    43→
    44→### Encoder options
    45→
    46→#### encode_html_chars
    47→
    48→Used to enable special encoding of "unsafe" HTML characters into safer Unicode
    49→sequences. Default is `False`:
    50→
    51→```pycon
    52→>>> ujson.dumps("<script>John&Doe", encode_html_chars=True)
    53→'"\\u003cscript\\u003eJohn\\u0026Doe"'
    54→```
    55→
    56→#### ensure_ascii
    57→
    58→Limits output to ASCII and escapes all extended characters above 127. Default is `True`.
    59→If your end format supports UTF-8, setting this option to false is highly recommended to
    60→save space:
    61→
    62→```pycon
    63→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö")
    64→'"\\u00e5\\u00e4\\u00f6"'
    65→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö", ensure_ascii=False)
    66→'"åäö"'
    67→```
    68→
    69→#### escape_forward_slashes
    70→
    71→Controls whether forward slashes (`/`) are escaped. Default is `True`:
    72→
    73→```pycon
    74→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com")
    75→'"https:\\/\\/example.com"'
    76→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com", escape_forward_slashes=False)
    77→'"https://example.com"'
    78→```
    79→
    80→#### indent
    81→
    82→Controls whether indentation ("pretty output") is enabled. Default is `0` (disabled):
    83→
    84→```pycon
    85→>>> ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"})
    86→'{"foo":"bar"}'
    87→>>> print(ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"}, indent=4))
    88→{
    89→    "foo": "bar"
    90→}
    91→```

   115→static char *PyUnicodeToUTF8Raw(JSOBJ _obj, size_t *_outLen, PyObject **pBytesObj)

   120→  In that case, the returned char* is in fact the internal buffer of that PyBytes object,
   121→  and when the char* buffer is no longer needed, the bytesObj must be DECREF'd.
   122→  */
   123→  PyObject *obj = (PyObject *) _obj;

   125→#ifndef Py_LIMITED_API

   134→
   135→  PyObject *bytesObj = *pBytesObj = PyUnicode_AsEncodedString (obj, NULL, "surrogatepass");
   136→  if (!bytesObj)

   138→    return NULL;
   139→  }

   141→  *_outLen = PyBytes_GET_SIZE(bytesObj);

   211→
   212→static PyObject* Dict_convertKey(PyObject* key)
   213→{
   214→  if (PyUnicode_Check(key))
   215→  {
   216→    return PyUnicode_AsEncodedString(key, NULL, "surrogatepass");
   217→  }
   218→  if (PyBytes_Check(key))
   219→  {
   220→    Py_INCREF(key);
   221→    return key;
   222→  }
   223→  if (UNLIKELY(PyBool_Check(key)))
   224→  {
   225→    return PyBytes_FromString(key == Py_True ? "true" : "false");
   226→  }
   227→  if (UNLIKELY(key == Py_None))
   228→  {
   229→    return PyBytes_FromString("null");
   230→  }
   231→  PyObject* keystr = PyObject_Str(key);
   232→  if (!keystr)
   233→  {
   234→    PRINTMARK();
   235→    return NULL;
   236→  }
   237→  key = PyUnicode_AsEncodedString(keystr, NULL, "surrogatepass");
   238→  Py_DECREF(keystr);
   239→  return key;
   240→}

   278→static int SortedDict_iterNext(JSOBJ obj, JSONTypeContext *tc)
   279→{
   280→  // Upon first call, obtain a list of the keys and sort them. This follows the same logic as the
   281→  // standard library's _json.c sort_keys handler.
   282→  if (GET_TC(tc)->newObj == NULL)
   283→  {
   284→    // Obtain the list of keys from the dictionary.
   285→    PyObject *keys = PyDict_Keys(GET_TC(tc)->dictObj);
   286→    if (keys == NULL)
   287→    {
   288→      return -1;
   289→    }
   290→    // Sort the list.
   291→    if (PyList_Sort(keys) < 0)
   292→    {
   293→      Py_DECREF(keys);
   294→      return -1;
   295→    }
   296→    // Store the sorted list of keys in the newObj slot.
   297→    GET_TC(tc)->newObj = keys;
   298→    GET_TC(tc)->size = PyList_GET_SIZE(keys);
   299→  }
   300→
   301→  if (GET_TC(tc)->index >= GET_TC(tc)->size)
   302→  {
   303→    PRINTMARK();
   304→    return 0;
   305→  }
   306→
   307→  PyObject* key = PyList_GET_ITEM(GET_TC(tc)->newObj, GET_TC(tc)->index);
   308→  Py_XDECREF(GET_TC(tc)->itemName);
   309→  GET_TC(tc)->itemName = Dict_convertKey(key);
   310→  if (!GET_TC(tc)->itemName)
   311→  {
   312→    return -1;
   313→  }
   314→  GET_TC(tc)->itemValue = PyDict_GetItem(GET_TC(tc)->dictObj, key);
   315→  if (!GET_TC(tc)->itemValue)
   316→  {
   317→    return -1;
   318→  }
   319→  GET_TC(tc)->index++;
   320→  return 1;
   321→}

   340→static void Object_beginTypeContext (JSOBJ _obj, JSONTypeContext *tc, JSONObjectEncoder *enc)
   341→{
   342→  PyObject *obj, *objRepr, *defaultFn, *newObj;
   343→  int level = 0;
   344→  TypeContext *pc;
   345→  PRINTMARK();
   346→  if (!_obj)
   347→  {
   348→    tc->type = JT_INVALID;
   349→    return;
   350→  }
   351→
   352→  obj = (PyObject*) _obj;
   353→  defaultFn = (PyObject*) enc->prv;
   354→
   355→  tc->prv = PyObject_Malloc(sizeof(TypeContext));
   356→  pc = (TypeContext *) tc->prv;
   357→  if (!pc)
   358→  {
   359→    tc->type = JT_INVALID;
   360→    PyErr_NoMemory();
   361→    return;
   362→  }
   363→  pc->newObj = NULL;
   364→  pc->dictObj = NULL;
   365→  pc->itemValue = NULL;
   366→  pc->itemName = NULL;
   367→  pc->index = 0;
   368→  pc->size = 0;
   369→  pc->longValue = 0;
   370→  pc->rawJSONValue = NULL;
   371→
   372→BEGIN:
   373→  if (PyIter_Check(obj))
   374→  {
   375→    PRINTMARK();
   376→    goto ISITERABLE;
   377→  }
   378→
   379→  if (PyBool_Check(obj))
   380→  {
   381→    PRINTMARK();
   382→    tc->type = (obj == Py_True) ? JT_TRUE : JT_FALSE;
   383→    return;
   384→  }
   385→  else
   386→  if (PyLong_Check(obj))
   387→  {
   388→    PRINTMARK();
   389→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyLongToINT64;
   390→    tc->type = JT_LONG;
   391→    GET_TC(tc)->longValue = PyLong_AsLongLong(obj);
   392→    if (!(GET_TC(tc)->longValue == -1 && PyErr_Occurred()))
   393→    {
   394→      return;
   395→    }
   396→    if (!PyErr_ExceptionMatches(PyExc_OverflowError))
   397→    {
   398→      goto INVALID;
   399→    }
   400→    PyErr_Clear();
   401→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyLongToUINT64;
   402→    tc->type = JT_ULONG;
   403→    GET_TC(tc)->unsignedLongValue = PyLong_AsUnsignedLongLong(obj);
   404→    if (!(GET_TC(tc)->unsignedLongValue == (unsigned long long)-1 && PyErr_Occurred()))
   405→    {
   406→      return;
   407→    }
   408→    if (!PyErr_ExceptionMatches(PyExc_OverflowError))
   409→    {
   410→      goto INVALID;
   411→    }
   412→    PyErr_Clear();
   413→    GET_TC(tc)->rawJSONValue = PyNumber_ToBase(obj, 10);
   414→    if (!GET_TC(tc)->rawJSONValue)
   415→    {
   416→      goto INVALID;
   417→    }
   418→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyLongToINTSTR;
   419→    tc->type = JT_RAW;
   420→    return;
   421→  }
   422→  else
   423→  if (UNLIKELY(PyBytes_Check(obj)))
   424→  {
   425→    PRINTMARK();
   426→    if (enc->rejectBytes)
   427→    {
   428→      PyErr_Format (PyExc_TypeError, "reject_bytes is on and '%s' is bytes", PyBytes_AS_STRING(obj));
   429→      goto INVALID;
   430→    }
   431→    else
   432→    {
   433→      pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyStringToUTF8; tc->type = JT_UTF8;
   434→      return;
   435→    }
   436→  }
   437→  else
   438→  if (PyUnicode_Check(obj))
   439→  {
   440→    PRINTMARK();
   441→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyUnicodeToUTF8; tc->type = JT_UTF8;
   442→    return;
   443→  }
   444→  else
   445→  if (obj == Py_None)
   446→  {
   447→    PRINTMARK();
   448→    tc->type = JT_NULL;
   449→    return;
   450→  }
   451→  else
   452→  if (PyFloat_Check(obj) || object_is_decimal_type(obj))
   453→  {
   454→    PRINTMARK();
   455→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyFloatToDOUBLE; tc->type = JT_DOUBLE;
   456→    return;
   457→  }
   458→
   459→ISITERABLE:
   460→  if (PyDict_Check(obj))
   461→  {
   462→    PRINTMARK();
   463→    tc->type = JT_OBJECT;
   464→    SetupDictIter(obj, pc, enc);
   465→    Py_INCREF(obj);
   466→    return;
   467→  }
   468→  else
   469→  if (PyList_Check(obj))
   470→  {
   471→    PRINTMARK();
   472→    tc->type = JT_ARRAY;
   473→    pc->iterEnd = List_iterEnd;
   474→    pc->iterNext = List_iterNext;
   475→    pc->iterGetValue = List_iterGetValue;
   476→    GET_TC(tc)->index =  0;
   477→    GET_TC(tc)->size = PyList_GET_SIZE( (PyObject *) obj);
   478→    return;
   479→  }
   480→  else
   481→  if (PyTuple_Check(obj))
   482→  {
   483→    PRINTMARK();
   484→    tc->type = JT_ARRAY;
   485→    pc->iterEnd = Tuple_iterEnd;
   486→    pc->iterNext = Tuple_iterNext;
   487→    pc->iterGetValue = Tuple_iterGetValue;
   488→    GET_TC(tc)->index = 0;
   489→    GET_TC(tc)->size = PyTuple_GET_SIZE( (PyObject *) obj);
   490→    GET_TC(tc)->itemValue = NULL;
   491→
   492→    return;
   493→  }
   494→
   495→  if (UNLIKELY(PyObject_HasAttrString(obj, "toDict")))
   496→  {
   497→    PyObject* toDictResult = PyObject_CallMethod(obj, "toDict", NULL);
   498→    if (toDictResult == NULL)
   499→    {
   500→      goto INVALID;
   501→    }
   502→
   503→    if (!PyDict_Check(toDictResult))
   504→    {
   505→      PyErr_Format(PyExc_TypeError, "toDict() should return a dict, got %s",
   506→                   Py_TYPE(toDictResult)->tp_name);
   507→      Py_DECREF(toDictResult);
   508→      goto INVALID;
   509→    }
   510→
   511→    PRINTMARK();
   512→    tc->type = JT_OBJECT;
   513→    SetupDictIter(toDictResult, pc, enc);
   514→    return;
   515→  }
   516→  else
   517→  if (UNLIKELY(PyObject_HasAttrString(obj, "__json__")))
   518→  {
   519→    PyObject* toJSONResult = PyObject_CallMethod(obj, "__json__", NULL);
   520→    if (toJSONResult == NULL)
   521→    {
   522→      goto INVALID;
   523→    }
   524→
   525→    if (!PyBytes_Check(toJSONResult) && !PyUnicode_Check(toJSONResult))
   526→    {
   527→      PyErr_Format(PyExc_TypeError, "__json__() should return str or bytes, got %s",
   528→                   Py_TYPE(toJSONResult)->tp_name);
   529→      Py_DECREF(toJSONResult);
   530→      goto INVALID;
   531→    }
   532→
   533→    PRINTMARK();
   534→    pc->PyTypeToJSON = PyRawJSONToUTF8;
   535→    tc->type = JT_RAW;
   536→    GET_TC(tc)->rawJSONValue = toJSONResult;
   537→    return;
   538→  }
   539→
   540→  if (defaultFn)
   541→  {
   542→    // Break infinite loop
   543→    if (level >= DEFAULT_FN_MAX_DEPTH)
   544→    {
   545→      PRINTMARK();
   546→      PyErr_Format(PyExc_TypeError, "maximum recursion depth exceeded");
   547→      goto INVALID;
   548→    }
   549→
   550→    newObj = PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs(defaultFn, obj, NULL);
   551→    if (newObj)
   552→    {
   553→      PRINTMARK();
   554→      Py_XDECREF(pc->newObj);
   555→      obj = pc->newObj = newObj;
   556→      level += 1;
   557→      goto BEGIN;
   558→    }
   559→    else
   560→    {
   561→      goto INVALID;
   562→    }
   563→  }
   564→
   565→  PRINTMARK();
   566→  PyErr_Clear();
   567→
   568→  objRepr = PyObject_Repr(obj);
   569→  if (!objRepr)
   570→  {
   571→    goto INVALID;
   572→  }
   573→  PyObject* str = PyUnicode_AsEncodedString(objRepr, NULL, "strict");
   574→  if (str)
   575→  {
   576→    PyErr_Format (PyExc_TypeError, "%s is not JSON serializable", PyBytes_AS_STRING(str));
   577→  }
   578→  Py_XDECREF(str);
   579→  Py_DECREF(objRepr);
   580→
   581→INVALID:
   582→  PRINTMARK();
   583→  tc->type = JT_INVALID;
   584→  PyObject_Free(tc->prv);
   585→  tc->prv = NULL;
   586→  return;
   587→}

   113→/*
   114→FIXME: Keep track of how big these get across several encoder calls and try to make an estimate
   115→That way we won't run our head into the wall each call */
   116→static void Buffer_Realloc (JSONObjectEncoder *enc, size_t cbNeeded)
   117→{
   118→  size_t free_space = enc->end - enc->offset;
   119→  if (free_space >= cbNeeded)
   120→  {
   121→    return;
   122→  }
   123→  size_t curSize = enc->end - enc->start;
   124→  size_t newSize = curSize;
   125→  size_t offset = enc->offset - enc->start;
   126→
   127→#ifdef DEBUG
   128→  // In debug mode, allocate only what is requested so that any miscalculation
   129→  // shows up plainly as a crash.
   130→  newSize = (enc->offset - enc->start) + cbNeeded;
   131→#else
   132→  while (newSize < curSize + cbNeeded)
   133→  {
   134→    newSize *= 2;
   135→  }
   136→#endif
   137→
   138→  if (enc->heap)
   139→  {
   140→    enc->start = (char *) enc->realloc (enc->start, newSize);
   141→    if (!enc->start)
   142→    {
   143→      SetError (NULL, enc, "Could not reserve memory block");
   144→      return;
   145→    }
   146→  }
   147→  else
   148→  {
   149→    char *oldStart = enc->start;
   150→    enc->heap = 1;
   151→    enc->start = (char *) enc->malloc (newSize);
   152→    if (!enc->start)
   153→    {
   154→      SetError (NULL, enc, "Could not reserve memory block");
   155→      return;
   156→    }
   157→    memcpy (enc->start, oldStart, offset);
   158→  }
   159→  enc->offset = enc->start + offset;
   160→  enc->end = enc->start + newSize;
   161→}
   162→
   163→#define Buffer_Reserve(__enc, __len) \
   164→    if ( (size_t) ((__enc)->end - (__enc)->offset) < (size_t) (__len))  \
   165→    {   \
   166→      Buffer_Realloc((__enc), (__len));\
   167→    }   \

   169→static void *Buffer_memcpy (JSONObjectEncoder *enc, const void *src, size_t n)
   170→{
   171→  void *out;
   172→#ifdef DEBUG
   173→  if ((size_t) (enc->end - enc->offset) < n) {
   174→    fprintf(stderr, "Ran out of buffer space during Buffer_memcpy()\n");
   175→    abort();
   176→  }
   177→#endif
   178→  out = memcpy(enc->offset, src, n);

   184→{

   186→  *(outputOffset++) = g_hexChars[(value & 0x0f00) >> 8];

   191→static int Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated (JSONObjectEncoder *enc, const char *io, const char *end)
   192→{
   193→  char *of = (char *) enc->offset;
   194→
   195→  for (;;)
   196→  {
   197→#ifdef DEBUG
   198→    // 6 is the maximum length of a single character (cf. RESERVE_STRING).
   199→    if ((io < end) && (enc->end - of < 6)) {
   200→      fprintf(stderr, "Ran out of buffer space during Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated()\n");
   201→      abort();
   202→    }
   203→#endif
   204→    switch (*io)
   205→    {
   206→      case 0x00:
   207→      {
   208→        if (io < end)
   209→        {
   210→          *(of++) = '\\';
   211→          *(of++) = 'u';
   212→          *(of++) = '0';
   213→          *(of++) = '0';
   214→          *(of++) = '0';
   215→          *(of++) = '0';
   216→          break;
   217→        }
   218→        else
   219→        {
   220→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   221→          return TRUE;
   222→        }
   223→      }
   224→      case '\"': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = '\"'; break;
   225→      case '\\': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = '\\'; break;
   226→      case '\b': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = 'b'; break;
   227→      case '\f': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = 'f'; break;
   228→      case '\n': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = 'n'; break;
   229→      case '\r': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = 'r'; break;
   230→      case '\t': (*of++) = '\\'; (*of++) = 't'; break;
   231→
   232→      case '/':
   233→      {
   234→        if (enc->escapeForwardSlashes)
   235→        {
   236→          (*of++) = '\\';
   237→          (*of++) = '/';
   238→        }
   239→        else
   240→        {
   241→          // Same as default case below.
   242→          (*of++) = (*io);
   243→        }
   244→        break;
   245→      }
   246→      case 0x26: // '&'
   247→      case 0x3c: // '<'
   248→      case 0x3e: // '>'
   249→      {
   250→        if (enc->encodeHTMLChars)
   251→        {
   252→          // Fall through to \u00XX case below.
   253→        }
   254→        else
   255→        {
   256→          // Same as default case below.
   257→          (*of++) = (*io);
   258→          break;
   259→        }
   260→      }
   261→      case 0x01:
   262→      case 0x02:
   263→      case 0x03:
   264→      case 0x04:
   265→      case 0x05:
   266→      case 0x06:
   267→      case 0x07:
   268→      case 0x0b:
   269→      case 0x0e:
   270→      case 0x0f:
   271→      case 0x10:
   272→      case 0x11:
   273→      case 0x12:
   274→      case 0x13:
   275→      case 0x14:
   276→      case 0x15:
   277→      case 0x16:
   278→      case 0x17:
   279→      case 0x18:
   280→      case 0x19:
   281→      case 0x1a:
   282→      case 0x1b:
   283→      case 0x1c:
   284→      case 0x1d:
   285→      case 0x1e:
   286→      case 0x1f:
   287→      {
   288→        *(of++) = '\\';
   289→        *(of++) = 'u';
   290→        *(of++) = '0';
   291→        *(of++) = '0';
   292→        *(of++) = g_hexChars[ (unsigned char) (((*io) & 0xf0) >> 4)];
   293→        *(of++) = g_hexChars[ (unsigned char) ((*io) & 0x0f)];
   294→        break;
   295→      }
   296→      default: (*of++) = (*io); break;
   297→    }
   298→    io++;
   299→  }
   300→}

   302→static int Buffer_EscapeStringValidated (JSOBJ obj, JSONObjectEncoder *enc, const char *io, const char *end)
   303→{
   304→  JSUTF32 ucs;
   305→  char *of = (char *) enc->offset;
   306→
   307→  for (;;)
   308→  {
   309→#ifdef DEBUG
   310→    /*
   311→    6 is the maximum length of a single character (cf. RESERVE_STRING).
   312→    Note that the loop below may consume more than one input char and produce a UTF-16 surrogate pair.
   313→    In that case, more than 6 characters would be needed on the output buffer.
   314→    So this calculates the maximum length of the entire remaining input buffer instead. */
   315→    if (enc->end - enc->offset < 6 * (end - io)) {
   316→      fprintf(stderr, "Ran out of buffer space during Buffer_EscapeStringValidated()\n");
   317→      abort();
   318→    }
   319→#endif
   320→    JSUINT8 utflen = g_asciiOutputTable[(unsigned char) *io];
   321→
   322→    switch (utflen)
   323→    {
   324→      case 0:
   325→      {
   326→        if (io < end)
   327→        {
   328→          *(of++) = '\\';
   329→          *(of++) = 'u';
   330→          *(of++) = '0';
   331→          *(of++) = '0';
   332→          *(of++) = '0';
   333→          *(of++) = '0';
   334→          io ++;
   335→          continue;
   336→        }
   337→        else
   338→        {
   339→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   340→          return TRUE;
   341→        }
   342→      }
   343→
   344→      case 1:
   345→      {
   346→        *(of++)= (*io++);
   347→        continue;
   348→      }
   349→
   350→      case 2:
   351→      {
   352→        JSUTF32 in;
   353→        JSUTF16 in16;
   354→
   355→        if (end - io < 1)
   356→        {
   357→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   358→          SetError (obj, enc, "Unterminated UTF-8 sequence when encoding string");
   359→          return FALSE;
   360→        }
   361→
   362→        memcpy(&in16, io, sizeof(JSUTF16));
   363→        in = (JSUTF32) in16;
   364→
   365→#ifdef __LITTLE_ENDIAN__
   366→        ucs = ((in & 0x1f) << 6) | ((in >> 8) & 0x3f);
   367→#else
   368→        ucs = ((in & 0x1f00) >> 2) | (in & 0x3f);
   369→#endif
   370→
   371→        if (ucs < 0x80)
   372→        {
   373→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   374→          SetError (obj, enc, "Overlong 2 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when encoding string");
   375→          return FALSE;
   376→        }
   377→
   378→        io += 2;
   379→        break;
   380→      }
   381→
   382→      case 3:
   383→      {
   384→        JSUTF32 in;
   385→        JSUTF16 in16;
   386→        JSUINT8 in8;
   387→
   388→        if (end - io < 2)
   389→        {
   390→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   391→          SetError (obj, enc, "Unterminated UTF-8 sequence when encoding string");
   392→          return FALSE;
   393→        }
   394→
   395→        memcpy(&in16, io, sizeof(JSUTF16));
   396→        memcpy(&in8, io + 2, sizeof(JSUINT8));
   397→#ifdef __LITTLE_ENDIAN__
   398→        in = (JSUTF32) in16;
   399→        in |= in8 << 16;
   400→        ucs = ((in & 0x0f) << 12) | ((in & 0x3f00) >> 2) | ((in & 0x3f0000) >> 16);
   401→#else
   402→        in = in16 << 8;
   403→        in |= in8;
   404→        ucs = ((in & 0x0f0000) >> 4) | ((in & 0x3f00) >> 2) | (in & 0x3f);
   405→#endif
   406→
   407→        if (ucs < 0x800)
   408→        {
   409→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   410→          SetError (obj, enc, "Overlong 3 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when encoding string");
   411→          return FALSE;
   412→        }
   413→
   414→        io += 3;
   415→        break;
   416→      }
   417→      case 4:
   418→      {
   419→        JSUTF32 in;
   420→
   421→        if (end - io < 3)
   422→        {
   423→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   424→          SetError (obj, enc, "Unterminated UTF-8 sequence when encoding string");
   425→          return FALSE;
   426→        }
   427→
   428→        memcpy(&in, io, sizeof(JSUTF32));
   429→#ifdef __LITTLE_ENDIAN__
   430→        ucs = ((in & 0x07) << 18) | ((in & 0x3f00) << 4) | ((in & 0x3f0000) >> 10) | ((in & 0x3f000000) >> 24);
   431→#else
   432→        ucs = ((in & 0x07000000) >> 6) | ((in & 0x3f0000) >> 4) | ((in & 0x3f00) >> 2) | (in & 0x3f);
   433→#endif
   434→        if (ucs < 0x10000)
   435→        {
   436→          enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   437→          SetError (obj, enc, "Overlong 4 byte UTF-8 sequence detected when encoding string");
   438→          return FALSE;
   439→        }
   440→
   441→        io += 4;
   442→        break;
   443→      }
   444→
   445→
   446→      case 5:
   447→      case 6:
   448→      {
   449→        enc->offset += (of - enc->offset);
   450→        SetError (obj, enc, "Unsupported UTF-8 sequence length when encoding string");
   451→        return FALSE;
   452→      }
   453→
   454→      case 29:
   455→      {
   456→        if (enc->encodeHTMLChars)
   457→        {
   458→          // Fall through to \u00XX case 30 below.
   459→        }
   460→        else
   461→        {
   462→          // Same as case 1 above.
   463→          *(of++) = (*io++);
   464→          continue;
   465→        }
   466→      }
   467→
   468→      case 30:
   469→      {
   470→        // \uXXXX encode
   471→        *(of++) = '\\';
   472→        *(of++) = 'u';
   473→        *(of++) = '0';
   474→        *(of++) = '0';
   475→        *(of++) = g_hexChars[ (unsigned char) (((*io) & 0xf0) >> 4)];
   476→        *(of++) = g_hexChars[ (unsigned char) ((*io) & 0x0f)];
   477→        io ++;
   478→        continue;
   479→      }
   480→      case 10:
   481→      case 12:
   482→      case 14:
   483→      case 16:
   484→      case 18:
   485→      case 20:
   486→      case 22:
   487→      {
   488→        *(of++) = *( (char *) (g_escapeChars + utflen + 0));
   489→        *(of++) = *( (char *) (g_escapeChars + utflen + 1));
   490→        io ++;
   491→        continue;
   492→      }
   493→      case 24:
   494→      {
   495→        if (enc->escapeForwardSlashes)
   496→        {
   497→          *(of++) = *( (char *) (g_escapeChars + utflen + 0));
   498→          *(of++) = *( (char *) (g_escapeChars + utflen + 1));
   499→          io ++;
   500→        }
   501→        else
   502→        {
   503→          // Same as case 1 above.
   504→          *(of++) = (*io++);
   505→        }
   506→        continue;
   507→      }
   508→      // This can never happen, it's here to make L4 VC++ happy
   509→      default:
   510→      {
   511→        ucs = 0;
   512→        break;
   513→      }
   514→    }
   515→
   516→    /*
   517→    If the character is a UTF8 sequence of length > 1 we end up here */
   518→    if (ucs >= 0x10000)
   519→    {
   520→      ucs -= 0x10000;
   521→      *(of++) = '\\';
   522→      *(of++) = 'u';
   523→      Buffer_AppendShortHexUnchecked(of, (unsigned short) (ucs >> 10) + 0xd800);
   524→      of += 4;
   525→
   526→      *(of++) = '\\';
   527→      *(of++) = 'u';
   528→      Buffer_AppendShortHexUnchecked(of, (unsigned short) (ucs & 0x3ff) + 0xdc00);
   529→      of += 4;
   530→    }
   531→    else
   532→    {
   533→      *(of++) = '\\';
   534→      *(of++) = 'u';
   535→      Buffer_AppendShortHexUnchecked(of, (unsigned short) ucs);
   536→      of += 4;
   537→    }
   538→  }
   539→}

   585→static void Buffer_AppendLongUnchecked(JSONObjectEncoder *enc, JSINT64 value)
   586→{
   587→  char* wstr;
   588→  JSUINT64 uvalue;
   589→
   590→  if (value == INT64_MIN) {
   591→    uvalue = INT64_MAX + UINT64_C(1);
   592→  } else {
   593→    uvalue = (value < 0) ? -value : value;
   594→  }
   595→
   596→  wstr = enc->offset;
   597→#ifdef DEBUG
   598→  // 20 is the maximum length of a JSINT64 (minus sign plus 19 digits)
   599→  if (enc->end - enc->offset < 20) {
   600→    fprintf(stderr, "Ran out of buffer space during Buffer_AppendLongUnchecked()\n");
   601→    abort();
   602→  }
   603→#endif
   604→  // Conversion. Number is reversed.
   605→
   606→  do *wstr++ = (char)(48 + (uvalue % 10ULL)); while(uvalue /= 10ULL);
   607→  if (value < 0) *wstr++ = '-';
   608→
   609→  // Reverse string
   610→  strreverse(enc->offset,wstr - 1);
   611→  enc->offset += (wstr - (enc->offset));
   612→}

   665→static void encode(JSOBJ obj, JSONObjectEncoder *enc, const char *name, size_t cbName)
   666→{
   667→  const char *value;
   668→  char *objName;
   669→  int count, res;
   670→  JSOBJ iterObj;
   671→  size_t szlen;
   672→  JSONTypeContext tc;
   673→
   674→  if (enc->level > enc->recursionMax)
   675→  {
   676→    SetError (obj, enc, "Maximum recursion level reached");
   677→    return;
   678→  }
   679→
   680→  if (enc->errorMsg)
   681→  {
   682→    return;
   683→  }
   684→
   685→  if (name)
   686→  {
   687→    Buffer_Reserve(enc, RESERVE_STRING(cbName) + enc->keySeparatorLength);
   688→    Buffer_AppendCharUnchecked(enc, '\"');
   689→
   690→    if (enc->forceASCII)
   691→    {
   692→      if (!Buffer_EscapeStringValidated(obj, enc, name, name + cbName))
   693→      {
   694→        return;
   695→      }
   696→    }
   697→    else
   698→    {
   699→      if (!Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated(enc, name, name + cbName))
   700→      {
   701→        return;
   702→      }
   703→    }
   704→
   705→    Buffer_AppendCharUnchecked(enc, '\"');

   167→                # Exclude ints because they get referenced by the lists below.
   168→                data_objects = [o for o in data_objects if not isinstance(o, int)]
   169→                gc.collect()
   170→                data_ref_counts_before = [sys.getrefcount(o) for o in data_objects]
   171→                ujson.dumps(data, **_options)
   172→                gc.collect()
   173→                data_ref_counts_after = [sys.getrefcount(o) for o in data_objects]
   174→                if data_ref_counts_before != data_ref_counts_after:
   175→                    for o, before, after in zip(
   176→                        data_objects, data_ref_counts_before, data_ref_counts_after
   177→                    ):
   178→                        if before != after:
   179→                            print(f"Ref count of {o!r} went from {before} to {after}")

   185→def collect_all_objects(obj):
   186→    """Given an object, return a list of all objects referenced by it."""
   187→
   188→    if hasattr(sys, "pypy_version_info"):
   189→        # PyPy's GC works differently (no ref counting), so this wouldn't be useful.
   190→        # Simply returning an empty list effectively disables the refcount test.
   191→        return []
   192→
   193→    def _inner(o):
   194→        yield o
   195→        if isinstance(o, list):
   196→            for v in o:
   197→                yield from _inner(v)
   198→        elif isinstance(o, dict):
   199→            for k, v in o.items():
   200→                yield from _inner(k)
   201→                yield from _inner(v)
   202→
   203→    out = []
   204→    seen = set()
   205→    for o in _inner(obj):
   206→        if id(o) not in seen:
   207→            seen.add(id(o))
   208→            out.append(o)
   209→    return out

TARGET 1: ujson.loads(obj) / ujson.decode(obj)
         [PRIMARY FUZZ TARGET - HIGHEST PRIORITY]
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Function signatures (from type stubs):
    def loads(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any
    def decode(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any

Both names are aliases for the same C function: JSONToObj()
  File: /app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c, line 163
  C signature: PyObject* JSONToObj(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)

How it works:
  1. Accepts one positional argument "obj" (PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords with "O")
  2. If input is bytes-like (supports buffer protocol): uses raw buffer
  3. If input is str (PyUnicode): encodes to UTF-8 via PyUnicode_AsEncodedString
  4. Otherwise: raises TypeError
  5. Initializes a JSONObjectDecoder with callback functions
  6. Calls JSON_DecodeObject() in ultrajsondec.c to do the actual parsing

Why this is a critical fuzz target:
  - Directly processes untrusted user input (arbitrary bytes/strings)
  - Written in C with manual memory management (malloc/realloc/free)
  - Complex parsing logic: string escaping, unicode handling (UTF-8 decoding,
    surrogate pair reconstruction), numeric parsing (int overflow detection,
    double-conversion library), recursive descent for nested structures
  - Has a history of buffer overflow vulnerabilities (per README warning)
  - The decoder handles: strings with escape sequences (\uXXXX, \n, etc.),
    numbers (int32, int64, uint64, bigint-from-string, doubles), booleans,
    null, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, arrays, objects
  - Escape buffer management in decode_string() with heap reallocation
  - UTF-8 multi-byte sequence validation (2, 3, 4 byte sequences)
  - Object depth tracking (JSON_MAX_OBJECT_DEPTH = 1024)

Input types to fuzz:
  - str: arbitrary Python strings, including surrogates, embedded NULs
  - bytes: arbitrary byte sequences, including invalid UTF-8
  - bytearray: arbitrary byte sequences

Acceptable exceptions:
  - ujson.JSONDecodeError (subclass of ValueError): all parse errors
  - TypeError: wrong argument type
  - UnicodeDecodeError / UnicodeEncodeError: encoding issues

Suspicious signals (indicate bugs):
  - Segfault / SIGSEGV / SIGABRT
  - SystemError
  - MemoryError on small inputs
  - Any exception type other than the acceptable ones above
  - AddressSanitizer / UBSan reports
  - Infinite loops / hangs

Areas of specific concern in the decoder:
  - decode_string() (ultrajsondec.c line 362): Complex escape handling,
    escape buffer reallocation, UTF-8 multi-byte validation, surrogate pair
    merging. The escOffset pointer writes to a dynamically sized buffer.
  - decode_numeric() (ultrajsondec.c line 91): Integer overflow handling,
    transitions to decodeDouble(), NaN/Infinity parsing. The hasError flag
    triggers newIntegerFromString for overflow cases.
  - decode_array/decode_object: Recursion depth tracking, object lifecycle
  - JSON_DecodeObject() entry point: escape buffer on stack initially
    (JSON_MAX_STACK_BUFFER_SIZE / sizeof(JSUINT32) = 256 entries), then
    heap-allocated if needed
  - The decodeDouble function casts (ds->end - ds->start) to int, capped at
    INT_MAX to prevent overflow

  File: /app/ujson/src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c, line 660
  C signature: PyObject* objToJSON(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)

How it works:
  1. Parses arguments: obj, ensure_ascii, encode_html_chars,
     escape_forward_slashes, sort_keys, indent, allow_nan, reject_bytes,
     default, separators
  2. Sets up JSONObjectEncoder struct with callback functions
  3. Uses a 65536-byte stack buffer initially; grows to heap if needed
  4. Calls JSON_EncodeObject() in ultrajsonenc.c
  5. Result is decoded from UTF-8 back to Python str

Why this is a good fuzz target:
  - Processes arbitrary Python objects through type dispatch
  - Complex string escaping logic (Buffer_EscapeStringValidated/Unvalidated)
  - UTF-8 validation during encoding (multi-byte sequence handling)
  - Buffer management with realloc (Buffer_Realloc)
  - Recursion through nested structures with depth limit
  - Multiple code paths based on kwargs (ensure_ascii, encode_html_chars, etc.)
  - The type dispatch in Object_beginTypeContext handles: bool, long (int32/
    int64/uint64/bigint), bytes, unicode, None, float, Decimal, dict, list,
    tuple, objects with toDict(), objects with __json__(), default function
  - Sort keys path (SortedDict_iterNext) vs unsorted path
  - Custom separators path
  - Default function with recursion depth limit (DEFAULT_FN_MAX_DEPTH = 3)

Input types to fuzz:
  - Any Python object: str, bytes, int, float, bool, None, list, dict, tuple,
    Decimal, custom objects with toDict()/__json__(), nested structures
  - Various combinations of keyword arguments
  - Very large integers (trigger bigint-from-string path)
  - Strings with special characters (surrogates, NUL bytes, control chars)
  - Deeply nested structures
  - Large indent values

Acceptable exceptions:
  - OverflowError: recursion limit, invalid double encoding, NaN/Inf with
    allow_nan=False
  - TypeError: non-serializable objects, wrong argument types, reject_bytes
  - ValueError: bad separators
  - RecursionError: cyclic references through toDict/default

Suspicious signals:
  - Segfault / SIGSEGV / SIGABRT
  - SystemError
  - MemoryError on small inputs
  - Any unexpected exception type
  - AddressSanitizer / UBSan reports

Areas of specific concern in the encoder:
  - Buffer_EscapeStringValidated() (ultrajsonenc.c line 302): Complex UTF-8
    multi-byte sequence handling with endian-dependent bit manipulation.
    Handles overlong sequence detection, unterminated sequences, and
    surrogate pair generation for supplementary plane characters.
  - Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated() (ultrajsonenc.c line 191): No UTF-8

  - Buffer_Realloc() (ultrajsonenc.c line 116): Doubling strategy for heap

  - Dict key conversion (Dict_convertKey): Handles str, bytes, bool, None,
    arbitrary objects via PyObject_Str
  - RESERVE_STRING macro: 2 + (len * 6) -- worst case for control chars

8. KNOWN VULNERABILITY AREAS (from code review)
================================================================================

a) String escape buffer in decoder (ultrajsondec.c, decode_string):
   - Initial escape buffer is on the stack (256 JSUINT32 entries)
   - Grows via realloc when input string is longer than buffer
   - Potential issues: integer overflow in size calculation (mitigated by
     SIZE_MAX check), use-after-free if realloc fails
   - Surrogate pair reconstruction modifies *(escOffset-1) which could
     underflow if a low surrogate appears at position 0

b) UTF-8 multi-byte handling in decoder (ultrajsondec.c, decode_string):
   - Manual UTF-8 decoding with continuation byte validation
   - Overlong sequence detection
   - Could read past buffer end if truncated multi-byte sequence at end of
     input (though NUL terminator from Python helps mitigate)

c) UTF-8 multi-byte handling in encoder (ultrajsonenc.c):
   - Buffer_EscapeStringValidated uses endian-dependent byte manipulation
   - Uses memcpy to load 2/3/4 bytes at a time, then bit-shifts
   - Could read past string end for truncated sequences (mitigated by
     length checks: end - io < N)

d) Integer parsing in decoder (ultrajsondec.c, decode_numeric):
   - Complex overflow detection logic for int64/uint64 boundaries
   - Falls back to newIntegerFromString for very large numbers
   - The hasError flag accumulation means some overflow can occur before
     being caught

e) Buffer management in encoder (ultrajsonenc.c):
   - Buffer_Realloc uses doubling strategy
   - RESERVE_STRING(len) = 2 + len*6 could overflow for very large len values
   - Buffer_AppendCharUnchecked has no bounds check (relies on prior Reserve)

f) Reference counting throughout objToJSON.c and JSONtoObj.c:
   - Complex ref counting across error paths
   - The README explicitly warns about security risks in the architecture

   342→def _make_help_call(target, esc):

   350→    t_magic_name, _, t_magic_arg_s = arg.partition(' ')

   407→class EscapedCommand(TokenTransformBase):
   408→    """Transformer for escaped commands like %foo, !foo, or /foo"""
   409→    @classmethod

   412→        """
   413→        for line in tokens_by_line:

   415→                continue
   416→            ix = 0
   417→            ll = len(line)
   418→            while ll > ix and line[ix].type in {tokenize.INDENT, tokenize.DEDENT}:
   419→                ix += 1
   420→            if ix >= ll:
   421→                continue
   422→            if line[ix].string in ESCAPE_SINGLES:
   423→                return cls(line[ix].start)

   426→        """Transform an escaped line found by the ``find()`` classmethod.
   427→        """
   428→        start_line, start_col = self.start_line, self.start_col
   429→
   430→        indent = lines[start_line][:start_col]
   431→        end_line = find_end_of_continued_line(lines, start_line)
   432→        line = assemble_continued_line(lines, (start_line, start_col), end_line)
   433→
   434→        if len(line) > 1 and line[:2] in ESCAPE_DOUBLES:
   435→            escape, content = line[:2], line[2:]
   436→        else:
   437→            escape, content = line[:1], line[1:]
   438→
   439→        if escape in tr:
   440→            call = tr[escape](content)
   441→        else:
   442→            call = ''

   444→        lines_before = lines[:start_line]
   445→        new_line = indent + call + '\n'
   446→        lines_after = lines[end_line + 1:]
   447→

   508→def make_tokens_by_line(lines:List[str]):

   520→    # track parentheses level, similar to the internals of tokenize.

   522→    #   reexported from token on 3.7+

   527→            "`make_tokens_by_line` received a list of lines which do not have lineending markers ('\\n', '\\r', '\\r\\n', '\\x0b', '\\x0c'), behavior will be unspecified",

   533→            iter(lines).__next__, extra_errors_to_catch=["expected EOF"]
   534→        ):

   537→                    or ((token.type == NL) and (parenlev <= 0)):
   538→                tokens_by_line.append([])
   539→            elif token.string in {'(', '[', '{'}:
   540→                parenlev += 1

   546→        pass

   556→def has_sunken_brackets(tokens: List[tokenize.TokenInfo]):

   563→            parenlev -= 1
   564→            if parenlev < 0:
   565→                return True

   594→    def do_one_token_transform(self, lines):

   600→        that all available transformations are complete.
   601→

   603→        the transformed code is retokenised every time to identify the next
   604→        piece of special syntax. Hopefully long code cells are mostly valid
   605→        Python, not using lots of IPython special syntax, so this shouldn't be
   606→        a performance issue.

   622→            except SyntaxError:

    65→def compress_dhist(dh):
    66→    """Compress a directory history into a new one with at most 20 entries.
    67→
    68→    Return a new list made from the first and last 10 elements of dhist after
    69→    removal of duplicates.
    70→    """
    71→    head, tail = dh[:-10], dh[-10:]
    72→
    73→    newhead = []
    74→    done = set()
    75→    for h in head:
    76→        if h in done:
    77→            continue
    78→        newhead.append(h)
    79→        done.add(h)
    80→
    81→    return newhead + tail

    95→def magics_class(cls):
    96→    """Class decorator for all subclasses of the main Magics class.
    97→
    98→    Any class that subclasses Magics *must* also apply this decorator, to
    99→    ensure that all the methods that have been decorated as line/cell magics
   100→    get correctly registered in the class instance.  This is necessary because
   101→    when method decorators run, the class does not exist yet, so they
   102→    temporarily store their information into a module global.  Application of
   103→    this class decorator copies that global data to the class instance and
   104→    clears the global.
   105→
   106→    Obviously, this mechanism is not thread-safe, which means that the
   107→    *creation* of subclasses of Magic should only be done in a single-thread
   108→    context.  Instantiation of the classes has no restrictions.  Given that
   109→    these classes are typically created at IPython startup time and before user
   110→    application code becomes active, in practice this should not pose any
   111→    problems.
   112→    """
   113→    cls.registered = True
   114→    cls.magics = dict(line=magics["line"], cell=magics["cell"])
   115→    magics["line"] = {}
   116→    magics["cell"] = {}
   117→    return cls

   120→def record_magic(dct, magic_kind, magic_name, func):
   121→    """Utility function to store a function as a magic of a specific kind.
   122→
   123→    Parameters
   124→    ----------
   125→    dct : dict
   126→        A dictionary with 'line' and 'cell' subdicts.
   127→    magic_kind : str
   128→        Kind of magic to be stored.
   129→    magic_name : str
   130→        Key to store the magic as.
   131→    func : function
   132→        Callable object to store.
   133→    """
   134→    if magic_kind == "line_cell":
   135→        dct["line"][magic_name] = dct["cell"][magic_name] = func
   136→    else:
   137→        dct[magic_kind][magic_name] = func

   140→def validate_type(magic_kind):
   141→    """Ensure that the given magic_kind is valid.
   142→
   143→    Check that the given magic_kind is one of the accepted spec types (stored
   144→    in the global `magic_spec`), raise ValueError otherwise.
   145→    """
   146→    if magic_kind not in magic_spec:
   147→        raise ValueError(
   148→            "magic_kind must be one of %s, %s given" % magic_kinds, magic_kind
   149→        )
   150→
   151→
   152→# The docstrings for the decorator below will be fairly similar for the two
   153→# types (method and function), so we generate them here once and reuse the
   154→# templates below.
   155→_docstring_template = """Decorate the given {0} as {1} magic.
   156→
   157→The decorator can be used with or without arguments, as follows.
   158→
   159→i) without arguments: it will create a {1} magic named as the {0} being
   160→decorated::
   161→
   162→    @deco
   163→    def foo(...)
   164→
   165→will create a {1} magic named `foo`.
   166→
   167→ii) with one string argument: which will be used as the actual name of the
   168→resulting magic::
   169→
   170→    @deco('bar')
   171→    def foo(...)
   172→
   173→will create a {1} magic named `bar`.
   174→
   175→To register a class magic use ``Interactiveshell.register_magic(class or instance)``.
   176→"""
   177→
   178→# These two are decorator factories.  While they are conceptually very similar,
   179→# there are enough differences in the details that it's simpler to have them
   180→# written as completely standalone functions rather than trying to share code
   181→# and make a single one with convoluted logic.
   182→
   183→
   184→def _method_magic_marker(magic_kind):
   185→    """Decorator factory for methods in Magics subclasses."""
   186→
   187→    validate_type(magic_kind)
   188→
   189→    # This is a closure to capture the magic_kind.  We could also use a class,
   190→    # but it's overkill for just that one bit of state.
   191→    def magic_deco(arg):
   192→        if callable(arg):
   193→            # "Naked" decorator call (just @foo, no args)
   194→            func = arg
   195→            name = func.__name__
   196→            retval = arg
   197→            record_magic(magics, magic_kind, name, name)
   198→        elif isinstance(arg, str):
   199→            # Decorator called with arguments (@foo('bar'))
   200→            name = arg
   201→
   202→            def mark(func, *a, **kw):
   203→                record_magic(magics, magic_kind, name, func.__name__)
   204→                return func
   205→
   206→            retval = mark
   207→        else:
   208→            raise TypeError("Decorator can only be called with string or function")
   209→        return retval
   210→
   211→    # Ensure the resulting decorator has a usable docstring
   212→    magic_deco.__doc__ = _docstring_template.format("method", magic_kind)
   213→    return magic_deco
   214→
   215→
   216→def _function_magic_marker(magic_kind):
   217→    """Decorator factory for standalone functions."""
   218→    validate_type(magic_kind)
   219→
   220→    # This is a closure to capture the magic_kind.  We could also use a class,
   221→    # but it's overkill for just that one bit of state.
   222→    def magic_deco(arg):
   223→        # Find get_ipython() in the caller's namespace
   224→        caller = sys._getframe(1)
   225→        for ns in ["f_locals", "f_globals", "f_builtins"]:
   226→            get_ipython = getattr(caller, ns).get("get_ipython")
   227→            if get_ipython is not None:
   228→                break
   229→        else:
   230→            raise NameError(
   231→                "Decorator can only run in context where `get_ipython` exists"
   232→            )
   233→
   234→        ip = get_ipython()
   235→
   236→        if callable(arg):
   237→            # "Naked" decorator call (just @foo, no args)
   238→            func = arg
   239→            name = func.__name__
   240→            ip.register_magic_function(func, magic_kind, name)
   241→            retval = arg
   242→        elif isinstance(arg, str):
   243→            # Decorator called with arguments (@foo('bar'))
   244→            name = arg
   245→
   246→            def mark(func, *a, **kw):
   247→                ip.register_magic_function(func, magic_kind, name)
   248→                return func
   249→
   250→            retval = mark
   251→        else:
   252→            raise TypeError("Decorator can only be called with string or function")
   253→        return retval
   254→
   255→    # Ensure the resulting decorator has a usable docstring
   256→    ds = _docstring_template.format("function", magic_kind)
   257→
   258→    ds += dedent(
   259→        """
   260→    Note: this decorator can only be used in a context where IPython is already
   261→    active, so that the `get_ipython()` call succeeds.  You can therefore use
   262→    it in your startup files loaded after IPython initializes, but *not* in the
   263→    IPython configuration file itself, which is executed before IPython is
   264→    fully up and running.  Any file located in the `startup` subdirectory of
   265→    your configuration profile will be OK in this sense.
   266→    """
   267→    )
   268→
   269→    magic_deco.__doc__ = ds
   270→    return magic_deco

   277→def no_var_expand(magic_func):
   278→    """Mark a magic function as not needing variable expansion
   279→
   280→    By default, IPython interprets `{a}` or `$a` in the line passed to magics
   281→    as variables that should be interpolated from the interactive namespace
   282→    before passing the line to the magic function.
   283→    This is not always desirable, e.g. when the magic executes Python code
   284→    (%timeit, %time, etc.).
   285→    Decorate magics with `@no_var_expand` to opt-out of variable expansion.
   286→
   287→    .. versionadded:: 7.3
   288→    """
   289→    setattr(magic_func, MAGIC_NO_VAR_EXPAND_ATTR, True)
   290→    return magic_func

   405→        """Return dict of documentation of magic functions.

   446→    def register(self, *magic_objects):
   447→        """Register one or more instances of Magics.
   448→
   449→        Take one or more classes or instances of classes that subclass the main
   450→        `core.Magic` class, and register them with IPython to use the magic
   451→        functions they provide.  The registration process will then ensure that
   452→        any methods that have decorated to provide line and/or cell magics will
   453→        be recognized with the `%x`/`%%x` syntax as a line/cell magic
   454→        respectively.
   455→
   456→        If classes are given, they will be instantiated with the default
   457→        constructor.  If your classes need a custom constructor, you should
   458→        instanitate them first and pass the instance.
   459→
   460→        The provided arguments can be an arbitrary mix of classes and instances.
   461→
   462→        Parameters
   463→        ----------
   464→        *magic_objects : one or more classes or instances
   465→        """
   466→        # Start by validating them to ensure they have all had their magic
   467→        # methods registered at the instance level
   468→        for m in magic_objects:
   469→            if not m.registered:
   470→                raise ValueError(
   471→                    "Class of magics %r was constructed without "
   472→                    "the @register_magics class decorator"
   473→                )
   474→            if isinstance(m, type):
   475→                # If we're given an uninstantiated class
   476→                m = m(shell=self.shell)
   477→
   478→            # Now that we have an instance, we can register it and update the
   479→            # table of callables
   480→            self.registry[m.__class__.__name__] = m
   481→            for mtype in magic_kinds:
   482→                self.magics[mtype].update(m.magics[mtype])

   484→    def register_function(self, func, magic_kind="line", magic_name=None):
   485→        """Expose a standalone function as magic function for IPython.
   486→
   487→        This will create an IPython magic (line, cell or both) from a
   488→        standalone function.  The functions should have the following
   489→        signatures:
   490→
   491→        * For line magics: `def f(line)`
   492→        * For cell magics: `def f(line, cell)`
   493→        * For a function that does both: `def f(line, cell=None)`
   494→
   495→        In the latter case, the function will be called with `cell==None` when
   496→        invoked as `%f`, and with cell as a string when invoked as `%%f`.
   497→
   498→        Parameters
   499→        ----------
   500→        func : callable
   501→            Function to be registered as a magic.
   502→        magic_kind : str
   503→            Kind of magic, one of 'line', 'cell' or 'line_cell'
   504→        magic_name : optional str
   505→            If given, the name the magic will have in the IPython namespace.  By
   506→            default, the name of the function itself is used.
   507→        """
   508→
   509→        # Create the new method in the user_magics and register it in the
   510→        # global table
   511→        validate_type(magic_kind)
   512→        magic_name = func.__name__ if magic_name is None else magic_name
   513→        setattr(self.user_magics, magic_name, func)
   514→        record_magic(self.magics, magic_kind, magic_name, func)

   516→    def register_alias(
   517→        self, alias_name, magic_name, magic_kind="line", magic_params=None
   518→    ):
   519→        """Register an alias to a magic function.
   520→
   521→        The alias is an instance of :class:`MagicAlias`, which holds the
   522→        name and kind of the magic it should call. Binding is done at
   523→        call time, so if the underlying magic function is changed the alias
   524→        will call the new function.
   525→
   526→        Parameters
   527→        ----------
   528→        alias_name : str
   529→            The name of the magic to be registered.
   530→        magic_name : str
   531→            The name of an existing magic.
   532→        magic_kind : str
   533→            Kind of magic, one of 'line' or 'cell'
   534→        """
   535→
   536→        # `validate_type` is too permissive, as it allows 'line_cell'
   537→        # which we do not handle.
   538→        if magic_kind not in magic_kinds:
   539→            raise ValueError(
   540→                "magic_kind must be one of %s, %s given" % magic_kinds, magic_kind
   541→            )

   551→class Magics(Configurable):
   552→    """Base class for implementing magic functions.
   553→
   554→    Shell functions which can be reached as %function_name. All magic
   555→    functions should accept a string, which they can parse for their own
   556→    needs. This can make some functions easier to type, eg `%cd ../`
   557→    vs. `%cd("../")`
   558→
   559→    Classes providing magic functions need to subclass this class, and they
   560→    MUST:
   561→
   562→    - Use the method decorators `@line_magic` and `@cell_magic` to decorate
   563→      individual methods as magic functions, AND
   564→
   565→    - Use the class decorator `@magics_class` to ensure that the magic
   566→      methods are properly registered at the instance level upon instance
   567→      initialization.
   568→
   569→    See :mod:`magic_functions` for examples of actual implementation classes.
   570→    """
   571→
   572→    # Dict holding all command-line options for each magic.
   573→    options_table: dict[str, t.Any] = {}
   574→    # Dict for the mapping of magic names to methods, set by class decorator
   575→    magics: dict[str, t.Any] = {}
   576→    # Flag to check that the class decorator was properly applied
   577→    registered: bool = False
   578→    # Instance of IPython shell
   579→    shell: None | InteractiveShell = None

   581→    def __init__(self, shell=None, **kwargs):
   582→        if not (self.__class__.registered):

   584→                "Magics subclass without registration - "
   585→                "did you forget to apply @magics_class?"

   589→                shell.configurables.append(self)

   592→

   594→        self.options_table = {}
   595→        # The method decorators are run when the instance doesn't exist yet, so
   596→        # they can only record the names of the methods they are supposed to
   597→        # grab.  Only now, that the instance exists, can we create the proper
   598→        # mapping to bound methods.  So we read the info off the original names
   599→        # table and replace each method name by the actual bound method.
   600→        # But we mustn't clobber the *class* mapping, in case of multiple instances.
   601→        class_magics = self.magics

   614→        # magics get screwed up.

   622→    def format_latex(self, strng):
   623→        """Format a string for latex inclusion."""
   624→
   625→        # Characters that need to be escaped for latex:
   626→        escape_re = re.compile(r"(%|_|\$|#|&)", re.MULTILINE)
   627→        # Magic command names as headers:
   628→        cmd_name_re = re.compile(r"^(%s.*?):" % ESC_MAGIC, re.MULTILINE)
   629→        # Magic commands
   630→        cmd_re = re.compile(r"(?P<cmd>%s.+?\b)(?!\}\}:)" % ESC_MAGIC, re.MULTILINE)
   631→        # Paragraph continue
   632→        par_re = re.compile(r"\\$", re.MULTILINE)

   634→        # The "\n" symbol
   635→        newline_re = re.compile(r"\\n")

   638→        # strng = cmd_name_re.sub(r'\n\\texttt{\\textsl{\\large \1}}:',strng)
   639→        strng = cmd_name_re.sub(r"\n\\bigskip\n\\texttt{\\textbf{ \1}}:", strng)
   640→        strng = cmd_re.sub(r"\\texttt{\g<cmd>}", strng)
   641→        strng = par_re.sub(r"\\\\", strng)
   642→        strng = escape_re.sub(r"\\\1", strng)

   646→    def parse_options(self, arg_str, opt_str, *long_opts, **kw):
   647→        """Parse options passed to an argument string.
   648→
   649→        The interface is similar to that of :func:`getopt.getopt`, but it
   650→        returns a :class:`~IPython.utils.struct.Struct` with the options as keys
   651→        and the stripped argument string still as a string.
   652→
   653→        arg_str is quoted as a true sys.argv vector by using shlex.split.
   654→        This allows us to easily expand variables, glob files, quote
   655→        arguments, etc.
   656→
   657→        Parameters
   658→        ----------
   659→        arg_str : str
   660→            The arguments to parse.
   661→        opt_str : str
   662→            The options specification.
   663→        mode : str, default 'string'
   664→            If given as 'list', the argument string is returned as a list (split
   665→            on whitespace) instead of a string.
   666→        list_all : bool, default False
   667→            Put all option values in lists. Normally only options
   668→            appearing more than once are put in a list.
   669→        posix : bool, default True
   670→            Whether to split the input line in POSIX mode or not, as per the
   671→            conventions outlined in the :mod:`shlex` module from the standard
   672→            library.
   673→        """
   674→
   675→        # inject default options at the beginning of the input line
   676→        caller = sys._getframe(1).f_code.co_name
   677→        arg_str = "%s %s" % (self.options_table.get(caller, ""), arg_str)
   678→
   679→        mode = kw.get("mode", "string")
   680→        if mode not in ["string", "list"]:
   681→            raise ValueError("incorrect mode given: %s" % mode)
   682→        # Get options
   683→        list_all = kw.get("list_all", 0)
   684→        posix = kw.get("posix", os.name == "posix")
   685→        strict = kw.get("strict", True)
   686→
   687→        preserve_non_opts = kw.get("preserve_non_opts", False)
   688→        remainder_arg_str = arg_str
   689→
   690→        # Check if we have more than one argument to warrant extra processing:
   691→        odict: dict[str, t.Any] = {}  # Dictionary with options
   692→        args = arg_str.split()
   693→        if len(args) >= 1:
   694→            # If the list of inputs only has 0 or 1 thing in it, there's no
   695→            # need to look for options
   696→            argv = arg_split(arg_str, posix, strict)
   697→            # Do regular option processing
   698→            try:
   699→                opts, args = getopt(argv, opt_str, long_opts)
   700→            except GetoptError as e:
   701→                raise UsageError(
   702→                    '%s (allowed: "%s"%s)'
   703→                    % (e.msg, opt_str, " ".join(("",) + long_opts) if long_opts else "")
   704→                ) from e
   705→            for o, a in opts:
   706→                if mode == "string" and preserve_non_opts:
   707→                    # remove option-parts from the original args-string and preserve remaining-part.
   708→                    # This relies on the arg_split(...) and getopt(...)'s impl spec, that the parsed options are
   709→                    # returned in the original order.
   710→                    remainder_arg_str = remainder_arg_str.replace(o, "", 1).replace(
   711→                        a, "", 1
   712→                    )
   713→                if o.startswith("--"):
   714→                    o = o[2:]
   715→                else:
   716→                    o = o[1:]
   717→                try:
   718→                    odict[o].append(a)
   719→                except AttributeError:
   720→                    odict[o] = [odict[o], a]
   721→                except KeyError:
   722→                    if list_all:
   723→                        odict[o] = [a]
   724→                    else:
   725→                        odict[o] = a
   726→
   727→        # Prepare opts,args for return
   728→        opts = Struct(odict)  # type: ignore[assignment]
   729→        if mode == "string":
   730→            if preserve_non_opts:
   731→                args = remainder_arg_str.lstrip()
   732→            else:
   733→                args = " ".join(args)
   734→
   735→        return opts, args

   745→class MagicAlias:
   746→    """An alias to another magic function.
   747→
   748→    An alias is determined by its magic name and magic kind. Lookup
   749→    is done at call time, so if the underlying magic changes the alias
   750→    will call the new function.
   751→

   753→    `%alias_magic` magic function to create and register a new alias.
   754→    """
   755→
   756→    def __init__(self, shell, magic_name, magic_kind, magic_params=None):
   757→        self.shell = shell
   758→        self.magic_name = magic_name
   759→        self.magic_params = magic_params
   760→        self.magic_kind = magic_kind
   761→
   762→        self.pretty_target = "%s%s" % (magic_escapes[self.magic_kind], self.magic_name)
   763→        self.__doc__ = "Alias for `%s`." % self.pretty_target
   764→
   765→        self._in_call = False

   767→    def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
   768→        """Call the magic alias."""
   769→        fn = self.shell.find_magic(self.magic_name, self.magic_kind)
   770→        if fn is None:

   774→        if self._in_call:

   779→        try:
   780→            if self.magic_params:
   781→                args_list = list(args)
   782→                args_list[0] = self.magic_params + " " + args[0]
   783→                args = tuple(args_list)
   784→            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
